classification.difficultyReason: Translate percentage changes into factors and choose cube roots for changes from q to p but cubes for changes from p to q, then interpret the resulting percentage changes.

content.prompt:
Given that $p\propto\sqrt[3]{q}$, what is the effect on:

All variables take positive values only. Give approximate percentage changes to 2 decimal places.

answer.worked:
Since $p=k\sqrt[3]{q}$, choose an original value $q=1$, giving $p=k$. After the increase, $q=1.1$.
$$\begin{align*}p_{\text{new}}&=k\sqrt[3]{1.1}\\\text{Percentage increase}&=(\sqrt[3]{1.1}-1)\times100\%\\\text{Percentage increase}&\approx3.23\%\end{align*}$$

Since $p=k\sqrt[3]{q}$, choose an original value $q=1$, giving $p=k$. After the decrease, $q=0.9$.
$$\begin{align*}p_{\text{new}}&=k\sqrt[3]{0.9}\\\text{Percentage decrease}&=(1-\sqrt[3]{0.9})\times100\%\\\text{Percentage decrease}&\approx3.45\%\end{align*}$$

$p=k\sqrt[3]{q}$ gives $q=\frac{p^3}{k^3}$. Choose an original value $p=1$, giving $q=\frac{1}{k^3}$. After the increase, $p=1.2$.
$$\begin{align*}q_{\text{new}}&=\frac{1.2^3}{k^3}\\q_{\text{new}}&=\frac{1.728}{k^3}\\\text{Percentage increase}&=(1.728-1)\times100\%\\\text{Percentage increase}&=72.8\%\end{align*}$$

$p=k\sqrt[3]{q}$ gives $q=\frac{p^3}{k^3}$. Choose an original value $p=1$, giving $q=\frac{1}{k^3}$. After the decrease, $p=0.8$.
$$\begin{align*}q_{\text{new}}&=\frac{0.8^3}{k^3}\\q_{\text{new}}&=\frac{0.512}{k^3}\\\text{Percentage decrease}&=(1-0.512)\times100\%\\\text{Percentage decrease}&=48.8\%\end{align*}$$
